page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 64 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz, this server utilizes the x86_64 architecture with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The processor includes a 33 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache, alongside hardware support for AVX-512 vector instructions and AES cryptography. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results position the n2-highmem-8 primarily in the average tier for multi-core processing and memory operations. The instance achieves average ratings in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, PassMark CPU scores, and memory bandwidth, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 413.33 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 40.05 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%. Computational bottlenecks are also visible in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, ray tracing, and image processing, which all rank in the weak category.

For specialized workloads, the instance delivers average performance in Redis SET operations (7.13 million operations per second), static web serving (7.05 GB/sec), and database operations. Conversely, language model tasks show significant limitations; while text generation with a small 135M model is average, prompt processing for a medium 7B model falls into the bottom 10% tier. Qualitatively, the n2-highmem-8 offers resource density optimized for memory-bound applications rather than raw compute or storage-heavy tasks. It is best suited for in-memory databases, caching layers, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring a larger memory footprint without the overhead of additional CPU cores.
